current_row.boundary_rationale: A third-person topic shift opens the row: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.” web:Job.6.14 (Hebrew לַמָּ֣ס מֵרֵעֵ֣הוּ חָ֑סֶד וְיִרְאַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י יַעֲזֽוֹב, oshb:Job.6.14, grammatically third-person throughout -- the friend-word carries a 3ms suffix and the verb is 3ms imperfect, with no vocative particle), pivoting the subject-matter from Job's own exhaustion to a gnomic charge against companions in general. He extends the charge with the brook-caravan metaphor, “My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;” web:Job.6.15, traces the image through the melting ice and vanishing caravans of web:Job.6.16-Job.6.20, then the address itself turns second-person for the first time in the unit, “For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.” web:Job.6.21 (Hebrew כִּֽי עַ֭תָּה הֱיִ֣יתֶם לא ל֑וֹ תִּֽרְא֥וּ חֲ֝תַ֗ת וַתִּירָֽאוּ, oshb:Job.6.21, all second-person plural), before closing on a pair of denials that he ever asked the friends for a gift or ransom, web:Job.6.22-Job.6.23. This second-person address shift at 6:21 is a genuine tier-1 signal, not mere texture; it runs unbroken to the end of the chapter, and it is disclosed here as a live internal candidate for this unit's own seam rather than dismissed. It is not adopted as the row's own edge because the third-person charge and its direct application are held together as one movement of the friend-rebuke closing on Job's self-examination through 6:23; the alternative seam at 6:20|6:21 is disclosed here as a live, comparably warranted rival rather than resolved.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking the row at Job.6.20|Job.6.21 for the second-person turn there is a live rival, not a texture-only consideration: 6:21 opens the unit's first 2mp forms and second-person address runs unbroken through 6:29 (nine verses, Job.6.21-Job.6.29), a comparably or better-warranted internal seam than the 6:23|6:24 edge kept here. It is disclosed rather than adopted because the row is held as one continuous rebuke of the friends across the third-person charge and its direct application; the question is left open rather than resolved, in the same spirit as the frame's own disclosed 2:6|2:7 crux.
current_row.literature_type_guess: friends rebuke: why abandon one brought low and helpless

items.claim: The row quotes the whole of oshb:Job.6.21 across the verse's ketiv/qere adjacency with no K/Q disclosure, then glosses the quoted string as 'all second-person plural'.
items.auditor_grounds: pmarks_Job.json kq registers 1 note at Job.6.21 (book total 53 notes / 49 verses, flagged HIGH), and the staged OSHB extract carries ketiv and qere ADJACENT inside the verse: the spliced pair is לא ל֑וֹ (ketiv unpointed, qere pointed), standing between the 2mp perfect and the 2mp imperfect. The row's quoted run reproduces the entire verse and therefore CROSSES that adjacency -- the canonical disclosure trigger (TOOLKIT wording, re-asserted at strategy §4). The quote is not byte-false (collate.py returns tier byte at oshb:Job.6.21), which is why the omission matters: a doubled reading is presented silently as continuous verse text, and the appended 'all second-person plural' gloss covers a string two of whose words -- the ketiv/qere pair -- are not second-person at all. The verse's three finite verbs ARE 2mp, so the person analysis holds; the defect is the missing K/Q disclosure and the over-wide gloss extent. Not load-bearing: the row's edges rest on 6:14 and 6:24, not on 6:21, and the 6:20|6:21 rival is disclosed either way.
items.proposed_change: Field repair only: inside the oshb:Job.6.21 parenthetical, disclose that the quoted span crosses the verse's ketiv/qere adjacency (WLC single-witness; ketiv and qere adjacent in the extract) and narrow the person gloss to the verse's three finite verbs. items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The quoted run therefore CROSSES the ketiv/qere adjacency, the canonical disclosure trigger (strategy section 4 and section 2e-b: disclose when a quoted span crosses the adjacency; TOOLKIT wording governs), and the shipped row carries no ketiv, qere or K/Q disclosure anywhere in boundary_rationale, boundary_evidence_refs or strongest_rejected_alternative (search of the shipped fields: zero hits). current_row.boundary_rationale: An explicit quotative frame opens this short strophe: אַחַ֗ת הִ֥יא עַל כֵּ֥ן (glossed ‘it is all one; therefore I say’, Job.9.22), introducing the indictment “he destroys the blameless and the wicked” web:Job.9.22. This opening word, תָּ֥ם (‘blameless’), repeats — at byte tier — the word that twice closes the preceding strophe's argument (תָּֽם at Job.9.20 word 5, תָּֽם at Job.9.21 word 1), a cross-seam lexical bond disclosed here rather than left implicit; it corroborates continuity of the courtroom-to-indictment argument across 9.21|9.22 without moving either strophe's edge. Job.9.23-Job.9.24 extend the same indictment: Job.9.22's מְכַלֶּֽה (‘destroys’) carries an explicit third-person subject, ה֣וּא, and Job.9.23's נְקִיִּ֣ם (‘mocks’) has no expressed subject of its own — WEB's own rendering keeps the pronoun 'he' across the verse boundary rather than naming 'the scourge' as a fresh subject, so the mocking agent is left as open a question in the Hebrew as in English; either way the indictment stays continuous, reaching “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked” web:Job.9.24, closing on the rhetorical question “If not he, then who is it?” web:Job.9.24. The subject shifts from this cosmic indictment to Job's own fleeting days at Job.9.25, marking the strophe's far edge.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding Job.9.22-Job.9.24 into the preceding courtroom-inability argument was rejected given the explicit inferential frame that opens Job.9.22 and the fresh third-person subject (earth, judges) it introduces.
current_row.literature_type_guess: theodicy indictment: God mocks the calamity of innocent

items.claim: The splice-plus-gloss 'Job.9.23's NEQIYIM (mocks)' names the wrong word: the token glossed is the plural noun 'innocent ones', not the mocking verb the argument needs.
items.auditor_grounds: oshb:Job.9.23 reads (word order) ... לְמַסַּ֖ת / נְקִיִּ֣ם / יִלְעָֽג. The spliced token נְקִיִּ֣ם is the masculine plural of naqi, 'innocent (ones)', standing as the nomen rectum after the construct לְמַסַּ֖ת ('at the trial of'); WEB 9:23 renders it 'the innocent' ('If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.'). The subjectless 3ms verb the claim actually depends on is יִלְעָֽג ('he will mock'), the verse's final word. The syntactic observation ('no expressed subject of its own') is true of that verb and cannot be true of a noun in a construct chain, so the warrant survives with the right token; the cited token and gloss do not. Byte-valid splice, semantically wrong word for the claim.
items.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale swap the splice and gloss to the verse-final verb of oshb:Job.9.23, יִלְעָֽג ('he will mock'), re-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json; the surrounding sentence otherwise stands.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. oshb:Job.9.23 reads אִם שׁ֭וֹט יָמִ֣ית פִּתְאֹ֑ם לְמַסַּ֖ת נְקִיִּ֣ם יִלְעָֽג: word 5 לְמַסַּ֖ת is a construct noun ('at the trial of'), word 6 נְקִיִּ֣ם is the masculine plural of naqi, 'innocent (ones)', its nomen rectum, and word 7 יִלְעָֽג, the verse-final word, is the 3ms yiqtol 'he mocks'; WEB “If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.” web:Job.9.23. The shipped sentence splices נְקִיִּ֣ם and glosses it 'mocks' while arguing that it 'has no expressed subject of its own', a predication that is true of the verb יִלְעָֽג and impossible for a noun inside a construct chain. The splice is byte-valid (collates BYTE at oshb:Job.9.23) but names the wrong word for the claim: a wrong-token splice as filed. The underlying continuity observation survives with the right token (the explicit 3ms subject ה֣וּא of מְכַלֶּֽה at oshb:Job.9.22 carries over to the subjectless יִלְעָֽג), so the row's edges and band are untouched: not load-bearing (not high), and a semantically wrong quoted word is a defective warrant rather than a mechanical slip (not low): medium confirmed. Repair proposal validated: swapping the splice and gloss to the verse-final verb יִלְעָֽג ('he will mock'), re-spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, matches the bytes; endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL only. both_sides_assessed false: the item concerns an intra-row token, not a seam.

current_row.boundary_rationale: Job turns from describing the assault to his own response to it, fronting the object of his mourning ritual: שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי עֲלֵ֣י גִלְדִּ֑י, “I have sewed sackcloth on my skin, and have thrust my horn in the dust.” (web:Job.16.15), continued in his physical distress, “My face is red with weeping. Deep darkness is on my eyelids,” (web:Job.16.16), and closing on a protest of innocence, “although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.” (web:Job.16.17). The preceding row's own opening also fronts a term before its verb (שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי, 'I was at ease,' Job.16.12), so word order alone does not distinguish this row's edge; what changes at Job.16.15 is Job's grammatical role, from the described object of a third-person assault (Job.16.9-Job.16.14) to the grammatical subject of his own 1cs acts (שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי, 'I have sewed') — a participant-role shift, not the fronting by itself, marks the topic turn to Job's own mourning and innocence, a short unit that ends before the vocative apostrophe to the earth opens the next row.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 16:15-17 as a continuation of the assault sequence would miss the fronted object that marks Job's own response as a new topic.
current_row.literature_type_guess: Weeping into dust with face-transformation imagery

items.claim: The row mislocates its cross-row comparison: Job.16.12 is the fourth verse of the preceding row, not that row's opening.
items.auditor_grounds: Shipped prev row M8-Job-063 span = Job.16.9-Job.16.14. Its opening verse MT Job.16.9 begins אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף - itself a subject fronted before its verb - so the comparison the row wants is available at the true opening and the underlying point (fronting is ambient here, hence non-distinctive as an edge signal) survives. What is false is only the locator: שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי is byte-exact at oshb:Job.16.12 (byte tier, sole book-wide hit) and Job.16.12 is verse four of the preceding row's six. The same verse also softens the row's other contrast, between 'the described object of a third-person assault (Job.16.9-Job.16.14)' and 'the grammatical subject of his own 1cs acts': הָיִ֨יתִי at oshb:Job.16.12 is itself a 1cs qatal inside the range said to hold Job as object.
items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): re-word to 'the preceding row's own opening also fronts a term before its verb (אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף, oshb:Job.16.9), as does Job.16.12 inside it', and add oshb:Job.16.9 to boundary_evidence_refs.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The adjacent preceding unit spans Job.16.9-Job.16.14 (six verses); its opening verse oshb:Job.16.9 begins אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף (byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide; a 3ms-suffixed subject noun fronted before its 3ms qatal verb, Job the 1cs object in וַֽיִּשְׂטְמֵ֗נִי), whereas שָׁ֘לֵ֤ו הָיִ֨יתִי is byte-exact at oshb:Job.16.12 only (sweep.py --heb: byte 1, skeleton 1) and Job.16.12 is that unit's FOURTH verse. The shipped locator 'the preceding row's own opening ... Job.16.12' is therefore false as a cross-row claim (E-18 arm), while the point it serves (fronting is ambient in the preceding unit, hence non-distinctive as an edge signal) is true at the real opening. The same verse softens the row's role contrast, as the auditor says: הָיִ֨יתִי is a 1cs qatal inside the range the row describes as holding Job as object. Both sides of the seam re-derive sound under the book's participant-shift rule: oshb:Job.16.14 closes יִפְרְצֵ֣נִי פֶ֭רֶץ עַל פְּנֵי פָ֑רֶץ יָרֻ֖ץ עָלַ֣י כְּגִבּֽוֹר (3ms verbs, Job the 1cs object in יִפְרְצֵ֣נִי and עָלַ֣י), and oshb:Job.16.15 opens שַׂ֣ק תָּ֭פַרְתִּי עֲלֵ֣י גִלְדִּ֑י וְעֹלַ֖לְתִּי בֶעָפָ֣ר קַרְנִֽי (fronted object plus 1cs qatal תָּ֭פַרְתִּי, then 1cs וְעֹלַ֖לְתִּי); the preceding unit names the same edge ('gives way to Job's own self-description of mourning at 16:15'), so the adjacent rows are coherent, and the far edge at oshb:Job.16.18 (אֶ֭רֶץ אַל תְּכַסִּ֣י, vocative plus 2fs jussive) is argued identically by the following unit. pmarks_Job.json records no PE or SAMEKH in chapter 16 (absence is not counterevidence). The defect is thus a false cross-row locator that is not load-bearing: medium confirmed (not high; not low because the claim is false, not merely workflow-phrased). Repair proposal validated: 'the preceding row's own opening also fronts a term before its verb (אַפּ֤וֹ טָרַ֨ף, oshb:Job.16.9), as does Job.16.12 inside it' matches the bytes, and adding oshb:Job.16.9 to boundary_evidence_refs anchors it; endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL with one qualification: the wording should be verse-anchored rather than positional ('the unit opening at Job.16.9') to satisfy section 10's register purge. both_sides_assessed true.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The speaker-change seam at Job.21.1|Job.22.1 opens this row: the previous row closes with Job answering (וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר, oshb:Job.21.1), and this row opens with Eliphaz answering instead (וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר, oshb:Job.22.1; “Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,” web:Job.22.1). The formula's epithet is spelled defectively here (הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י) against the fuller spelling Eliphaz's first two formula instances carry (הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י, oshb:Job.4.1 and oshb:Job.15.1); swept independently, the defective spelling occurs at Job.22.1 alone (sweep: 1 book-wide) while the fuller spelling occurs 5 times book-wide, both in formula position and in narration (oshb:Job.2.11, oshb:Job.4.1, oshb:Job.15.1, oshb:Job.42.7, oshb:Job.42.9). Four verse-initial ha-interrogative tokens open this row in sequence — הַלְאֵ֥ל (Job.22.2), הַחֵ֣פֶץ (Job.22.3), הֲֽ֭מִיִּרְאָ֣תְךָ (Job.22.4), הֲלֹ֣א (Job.22.5) — the first three of which WEB's own punctuation further unpacks into four question-marked clauses, since Job.22.3's second colon (וְאִם בֶּ֝֗צַע כִּֽי תַתֵּ֥ם דְּרָכֶֽיךָ) is also rendered as a question though it opens on a mid-verse וְאִם rather than a fresh he-token; Job.22.5's הֲלֹ֣א (oshb:Job.22.5) sharpens the charge from piety to outright wickedness, setting up the itemized list that follows without yet stating it. Eliphaz's fifth and final ha-interrogative in this speech falls outside this row, at Job.22.12.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the row at Job.22.4 and treating Job.22.5 as an opening line of the accusation catalogue was rejected, since Job.22.5 is still framed as an interrogative continuing the ha-prefixed question series of Job.22.2-Job.22.4, against the declarative register the catalogue itself uses from Job.22.6 on — a register contrast, not an asyndetic one: three of the catalogue's six verses (Job.22.6, Job.22.8, Job.22.11) open on overt connectives (כִּֽי, וְאִ֣ישׁ, אוֹ) rather than asyndetically, Job.22.6 itself a subordinating ki-clause.
current_row.literature_type_guess: Eliphaz's third-cycle response opening with piety-premise

items.claim: The opening-seam sentence mis-notates the seam (Job.21.1|Job.22.1 for Job.21.34|Job.22.1) and mis-describes the previous row as closing with the vaya'an of Job.21.1.
items.auditor_grounds: Prev row M8-Job-088 span = Job.21.27-Job.21.34; MT Job.21.1 (וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר, byte tier, one of the nine book-wide members of the generic Job-reply formula) sits 26 verses before that row's first verse and opens Job's speech, not any row's close. The corpus uses X|Y for ADJACENT verses - this same slice writes 'Job.22.25|Job.22.26' and 'Job.22.24|Job.22.25' - so 'Job.21.1|Job.22.1' is a wrong-seam cite. The seam itself is unaffected and correct: MT Job.22.1 carries the speaker-change formula וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר (byte tier at oshb:Job.22.1, sole book-wide hit), and the prev row independently corroborates its own close with the SAMEKH after Job.21.34.
items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): 'The speaker-change seam at Job.21.34|Job.22.1 opens this row: Job's speech, opened by וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר at oshb:Job.21.1, ends at Job.21.34, and this row opens with Eliphaz answering, וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר (oshb:Job.22.1)'.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The adjacent preceding unit spans Job.21.27-Job.21.34 and closes at oshb:Job.21.34, וְ֭אֵיךְ תְּנַחֲמ֣וּנִי הָ֑בֶל וּ֝תְשֽׁוּבֹתֵיכֶ֗ם נִשְׁאַר מָֽעַל, a 2mp address to the friends (תְּנַחֲמ֣וּנִי, וּ֝תְשֽׁוּבֹתֵיכֶ֗ם) followed by SAMEKH (pmarks_Job.json marks[Job.21.34] = SAMEKH, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only); oshb:Job.21.1, וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר, collates BYTE and is one of the nine book-wide members of the generic Job-reply formula (byte sweep: 9 verses), standing 26 verses before that unit's first verse as the opening of Job's speech, not any unit's close. The row opens at oshb:Job.22.1 on the speaker-change formula וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר (BYTE, sole book-wide hit), so the seam is Job.21.34|Job.22.1 under the explicit speaker-change rule, with the SAMEKH corroborating; the adjacent unit argues the same seam ('immediately before Eliphaz's third-speech formula opens at 22:1'), so the two rows are coherent. The shipped sentence is false twice over: 'the previous row closes with Job answering (וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר, oshb:Job.21.1)' misdescribes the adjacent unit's close (E-18 arm), and 'Job.21.1|Job.22.1' pairs verses 34 apart in the pipe notation this corpus uses for adjacent verses (the slice's own rows write Job.6.20|Job.6.21, Job.9.27|Job.9.28, 6:23|6:24). The seam and its warrant are unaffected, so the defect is not load-bearing (not high), and a byte-false cross-row claim is more than a register slip (not low): medium confirmed. Repair proposal validated: 'The speaker-change seam at Job.21.34|Job.22.1 opens this row: Job's speech, opened by וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר at oshb:Job.21.1, ends at Job.21.34, and this row opens with Eliphaz answering, וַ֭יַּעַן אֱלִיפַ֥ז הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר (oshb:Job.22.1)' matches the bytes above, the speech-end claim resting on the 22:1 formula with the SAMEKH as tier-3 corroboration; endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL only. both_sides_assessed true.

items.claim: 'Eliphaz's fifth and final ha-interrogative in this speech falls outside this row, at Job.22.12' is byte-false as to 'final': a sixth verse-initial interrogative he opens Job.22.15.
items.auditor_grounds: Re-swept over the first word of every verse of Eliphaz's third speech (MT Job.22.2-Job.22.30) in verse_map_oshb.json. Verse-initial interrogative he: Job.22.2 הַלְאֵ֥ל, Job.22.3 הַחֵ֣פֶץ, Job.22.4 הֲֽ֭מִיִּרְאָ֣תְךָ, Job.22.5 הֲלֹ֣א, Job.22.12 הֲֽלֹא and Job.22.15 הַאֹ֣רַח - six members, so Job.22.12 is correctly the FIFTH but is not the final one. WEB Job.22.15 confirms the interrogative reading ('Will you keep the old way, which wicked men have trodden,'), the question running on into Job.22.16 so that no question mark falls inside Job.22.15 itself. The two near-miss verse-initial he-tokens are correctly excluded from the series: Job.22.17's הָאֹמְרִ֣ים is the qamats-he ARTICLE on a participle and Job.22.21's הַסְכֶּן is a hiphil imperative. Not load-bearing - the claim sits beyond the row's far edge and neither the seam nor the rival's rejection rests on it. (The row's other digits in this field re-derive TRUE: the defective Temanite spelling sweeps 1 book-wide, at Job.22.1 alone, and the fuller spelling 5 book-wide at Job.2.11, Job.4.1, Job.15.1, Job.42.7 and Job.42.9, exactly the members listed - a spelling-level, not byte-level, object, the pointed form הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י at oshb:Job.22.1 being a byte singleton and הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י standing byte-identically at oshb:Job.4.1 and oshb:Job.15.1 only.)
items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY (field repair, no span change): 'Eliphaz's fifth ha-interrogative falls outside this row at Job.22.12, and a sixth and final one opens Job.22.15 (הַאֹ֣רַח, oshb:Job.22.15).'
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes: the first word of every verse of Eliphaz's third speech, oshb:Job.22.2-Job.22.30, read from verse_map_oshb.json (count object: verse-initial interrogative he, exhaustive over the 29 verses). Members: Job.22.2 הַלְאֵ֥ל, Job.22.3 הַחֵ֣פֶץ, Job.22.4 הֲֽ֭מִיִּרְאָ֣תְךָ, Job.22.5 הֲלֹ֣א, Job.22.12 הֲֽלֹא, Job.22.15 הַאֹ֣רַח: six. The only other he-initial verses are correctly non-members: Job.22.17 הָאֹמְרִ֣ים carries the qamats article on a participle, and Job.22.21 הַסְכֶּן is a hiphil imperative (WEB renders it as the imperative 'Acquaint yourself with him now'); no verse from 22:16 to 22:30 opens on a further interrogative he. Job.22.15 is interrogative in form (patah he before aleph, where the article would take qamats) and in rendering, “Will you keep the old way, which wicked men have trodden,” web:Job.22.15. So Job.22.12 is correctly the FIFTH member but 'final' is byte-false: a false exclusivity claim (E-05). Not load-bearing (the claim sits beyond the row's far edge; the opening seam rests on the formula at oshb:Job.22.1 and the far-edge rejection on הֲלֹ֣א at oshb:Job.22.5 and the connectives כִּֽי, וְאִ֣ישׁ, אוֹ), so not high; a false digit-class claim is not a mere disclosure gap, so not low: medium confirmed. The row's other digits in the same field re-derive TRUE with their objects named: הַֽתֵּמָנִ֗י byte sweep 1 (Job.22.1; skeleton 1), הַֽתֵּימָנִ֗י byte sweep 2 (Job.4.1, Job.15.1) and skeleton sweep 5 (Job.2.11, Job.4.1, Job.15.1, Job.42.7, Job.42.9), so the row's '5 times book-wide' is a spelling-level count, matching WEB 'Temanite' 6 verses = 5 + 1. Repair proposal validated: 'Eliphaz's fifth ha-interrogative falls outside this row at Job.22.12, and a sixth and final one opens Job.22.15 (הַאֹ֣רַח, oshb:Job.22.15)' is exact against the exhaustive sweep; endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL only. both_sides_assessed false: a count-object item that concerns no seam.

current_row.boundary_rationale: Address shifts from third-person description of the wicked to direct second-person imperative: הַסְכֶּן נָ֣א (oshb:Job.22.21, “Acquaint yourself with him now, and be at peace” web:Job.22.21), opening Eliphaz's closing appeal. The conditional particle אִם (oshb:Job.22.23) then sets the return-to-Shaddai protasis whose apodosis promises being built up, and the appeal continues through the treasure-exchange imagery of Job.22.24-Job.22.25 (laying gold in the dust in exchange for Shaddai himself as treasure).
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping Job.22.21-Job.22.30 together as one ten-verse appeal was rejected in favor of a split at Job.22.25, though the chain's own consequent clause is already running by that point — וְהָיָ֣ה שַׁדַּ֣י בְּצָרֶ֑יךָ (Job.22.25) is itself a waw-qatal result clause, not a further protasis — and Job.22.26's own consequence particle simply continues that same result movement rather than opening a fresh one, so no clause-type boundary marks Job.22.25|Job.22.26 itself. The appeal's imperative-to-promise register shift (imperative at Job.22.21 and Job.22.23-Job.22.24, promise from Job.22.25 on) in fact falls one verse earlier, inside this row's own span, rather than at its Job.22.25|Job.22.26 close; the retained split is kept as a topical break within the continuous appeal-to-promise material, disclosed as weaker than a fresh clause-type opening.

current_row.boundary_rationale: כִּי אָ֭ז (oshb:Job.22.26, “For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty” web:Job.22.26) continues, rather than reopens, the unbroken veqatal/result chain running from Job.22.23's protasis (אִם תָּשׁ֣וּב עַד שַׁ֭דַּי תִּבָּנֶ֑ה) through Job.22.24's imperative and Job.22.25's own waw-qatal consequent (וְהָיָ֣ה שַׁדַּ֣י בְּצָרֶ֑יךָ); no renewed protasis, address-shift, or formula marks Job.22.25|Job.22.26 itself. This row's material — delight in Shaddai, answered prayer, decreed authority, and rescue for the humble — closes the speech at Job.22.30 on the strength of that continuous chain; the appeal's own imperative-to-promise register shift, disclosed as this row's best available ground, in fact falls one verse earlier, at Job.22.24|Job.22.25 inside the preceding row (as at Job.22.21-Job.22.25), so it continues unbroken across this row's own opening rather than marking it. A petuchah follows Job.22.30 (oshb:Job.22.30 (petuchah, single-witness)), corroborating - at Writings-tier-3 weak strength, not as a driver - a break at the chapter's end, where Job's own vaya'an formula opens the next row.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this row back into Job.22.21-Job.22.25 was declined not because Job.22.26 opens a distinct result movement — the veqatal chain from Job.22.23 runs unbroken through it — but because doing so would erase the petuchah's (single-witness) association with the speech's own genuine closing edge at Job.22.30, and because the register shift from imperative appeal (Job.22.21-Job.22.24) to sustained promise (from Job.22.25 on) still offers a defensible, if weaker, internal seam near this row's own opening.

items.claim: By the row's own byte analysis its opening seam at Job.22.25|Job.22.26 carries no signal of any tier, and the sole ground offered for retaining it - preserving the petuchah's association with Job.22.30 - is a non-sequitur.
items.auditor_grounds: Re-derived from bytes: MT Job.22.23 opens the protasis אִם תָּשׁ֣וּב, Job.22.24 continues on the imperative וְשִׁית, Job.22.25 is the waw-qatal consequent וְהָיָ֣ה, and Job.22.26 opens כִּי אָ֭ז - a continuation particle inside that same result chain, exactly as the row itself states ('no renewed protasis, address-shift, or formula marks Job.22.25|Job.22.26 itself'). All of Job.22.21-Job.22.30 is one unbroken 2ms address with no vocative, no speech formula and no parashah mark until the PE that pmarks_Job.json records after Job.22.30 (marks[Job.22.30] = PE - petuchah, single-witness, Writings tier-3 weak corroboration only; the row's mark type and cite form are correct). The row's second retention ground is placed by the row itself one verse earlier, inside the preceding row (וְשִׁית at oshb:Job.22.24 to וְהָיָ֣ה at oshb:Job.22.25), so it cannot mark this row's opening. The petuchah ground does not follow: a merged Job.22.21-Job.22.30 row would still close at Job.22.30, where the petuchah stands, so merging erases nothing. Job's owner-ruled strategy section 6 seams rows at tier-1 signals ONLY, and the confidence label 'medium' is over-stated for a seam the row concedes is unmarked. Cross-row check: the preceding row M8-Job-092 concedes the same thing in its own strongest_rejected_alternative, so the two neighbours are coherent with each other but jointly retain an unwarranted seam.
items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY - routes onward to adjudication, no edit made. Either (a) merge M8-Job-092 and M8-Job-093 into one row Job.22.21-Job.22.30, whose close the petuchah at oshb:Job.22.30 still corroborates at Writings tier-3; or (b) move the seam to Job.22.24|Job.22.25 where the row itself locates the imperative-to-promise shift, giving Job.22.21-Job.22.24 plus Job.22.25-Job.22.30. If the shipped split is retained, drop the petuchah-erasure reasoning from strongest_rejected_alternative and cap confidence at medium_low.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways; every Hebrew run below is spliced from verse_map_oshb.json and collates at BYTE tier; Job 22-23 lie outside the offset zone (job_lib crosswalk: identity), so MT and WEB numbering coincide. The shipped seam Job.22.25|Job.22.26 carries no ruled tier-1 signal on either side. Preceding unit's closing verse oshb:Job.22.25: וְהָיָ֣ה שַׁדַּ֣י בְּצָרֶ֑יךָ וְכֶ֖סֶף תּוֹעָפ֣וֹת לָֽךְ (web:Job.22.25 “The Almighty will be your treasure, and precious silver to you.”) - a waw-qatal consequent continuing the conditional chain that opens at oshb:Job.22.23 אִם תָּשׁ֣וּב עַד שַׁ֭דַּי תִּבָּנֶ֑ה (the pointed string אִם תָּשׁ֣וּב sweeps 1 book-wide at byte tier) and runs through the imperative at oshb:Job.22.24 וְשִׁית עַל עָפָ֥ר בָּ֑צֶר. Following unit's opening verse oshb:Job.22.26: כִּי אָ֭ז עַל שַׁדַּ֣י תִּתְעַנָּ֑ג וְתִשָּׂ֖א אֶל אֱל֣וֹהַּ פָּנֶֽיךָ (web:Job.22.26 “For then you will delight yourself in the Almighty, and will lift up your face to God.”) - the result-continuation pair כִּי אָ֭ז (byte sweep: 1; skeleton sweep: 5 book-wide, an ambient connective), with no vocative, no fresh protasis, no interrogative, no speech formula and no participant or scene shift. The 2ms address runs unbroken from the imperative הַסְכֶּן נָ֣א at oshb:Job.22.21 (byte sweep: 1 book-wide) to כַּפֶּֽיךָ closing oshb:Job.22.30; pmarks_Job.json records no parashah mark and no ketiv/qere note anywhere in Job.22.21-Job.22.29 (chapter 22's sole mark is the PE after Job.22.30 - oshb:Job.22.30 (petuchah, single-witness), tier-3 weak corroboration, correctly typed by the row; paseq is count-only and irrelevant to the seam). The row concedes the same in its own words ('no renewed protasis, address-shift, or formula marks Job.22.25|Job.22.26 itself'); under strategy section 6 rows are seamed at tier-1 signals ONLY and a topical break is texture, so the opening boundary is unwarranted and the defect is load-bearing: high stands. Both retention grounds fail from bytes: the imperative-to-promise shift the row names falls at Job.22.24|Job.22.25, inside M8-Job-092's own span Job.22.21-Job.22.25, so it cannot mark Job.22.26; and the petuchah-erasure reasoning is a non-sequitur, since a merged Job.22.21-Job.22.30 row still closes at Job.22.30 where the mark stands, and as written it lets a tier-3 mark five verses away act as a seam driver.
